overview: This file assembles U.S. wartime intelligence and policy analysis on Japan’s economic position, imperial system, and prospective postwar settlement. Its documents assess shortages and uses of strategic materials; report on food, transport, industry, and daily life in Japan and its empire; examine Japanese political control, resource extraction, currency manipulation, and collaborationist institutions in occupied China and Southeast Asia; and trace State Department debates over economic disarmament, reparations, industrial controls, subsistence, and eventual reintegration into world trade. Together, they show officials moving from the study of Japan’s wartime vulnerabilities and colonial exploitation toward detailed planning for occupation and the construction of a peaceful but economically viable postwar Japan.
interest: Wartime shortage intelligence beside drafts for governing postwar Japan, debating how to end war-making capacity without mass poverty.
